# Reference: golden vectors

Byte-exact test vectors for the `terrane-v1` profile. Every vector below was
generated from the rules in the owning file and is normative when a
requirement cites it ([`../00-conventions.md`](../00-conventions.md)).
An implementation MUST reproduce each positive vector exactly and reject
each explicitly negative vector through its format decoder; `gate:golden-vectors`
([`../36-testing-and-conformance.md`](../36-testing-and-conformance.md)
TEST-1) checks every one.

Hex is lowercase. CBOR is shown in diagnostic notation and as the exact
canonical bytes ([`../06-tree-format.md`](../06-tree-format.md) TREE-25).
Identities are BLAKE3-256 over `domain || 0x00 || bytes`
([`../04-content-model.md`](../04-content-model.md) OBJ-2). Signatures use
Ed25519 with the RFC 8032 §7.1 test keys so that any implementation can
regenerate them.

conformance suite.

## Gear table

The FastCDC gear table ([`../05-chunking.md`](../05-chunking.md) CDC-1) is
derived from the profile seed:

```text
bytes   = BLAKE3-XOF( "terrane-gear-v1" || 0x00 || seed, 2048 bytes )
gear[i] = u64le( bytes[8*i .. 8*i + 8] )        for i in 0 .. 256
```

The `cdc-1m` vectors ([`property-registry.md`](property-registry.md)
§chunk profiles) use the all-zero 32-byte seed. A store uses its recorded
seed (CDC-2); these witnesses do not restrict that seed. For the vector seed:

| i | `gear[i]` |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | `0x15f23553a70da356` |
| 1 | `0x9700318b430e40f3` |
| 2 | `0x70cd1174e9697d43` |
| 3 | `0x0026abb73a8487ac` |
| 4 | `0xae9e6f49c0846cb3` |
| 5 | `0xafd4bb99913bf95f` |
| 6 | `0xba377b75cd23033d` |
| 7 | `0xb0cd9e1ce544864c` |

BLAKE3 of the full 2 048-byte table: `22e8d10aa13d65d681fa4ff159d1151c11c90f652bc059d4418c3f463f49b14c`.

For the `cdc-1m` profile, the two level-2 masks derived by CDC-1 are
`0x0000b6db6db70000` up to and including 1 MiB and
`0x0000aab556ab0000` above 1 MiB. Generate a 16,777,216-byte input with
`BLAKE3-XOF("terrane-cdc-boundaries-v1" || 0x00)` and cut it from offset zero
using the all-zero profile seed. The cumulative end offsets, including EOF,
are:

```text
1,053,018   1,336,528   2,676,886   3,833,803   4,242,108
5,460,736   6,765,165   8,343,797   9,434,089  10,501,272
11,945,946  13,357,494  15,153,770  16,005,372  16,777,216
```

`gate:cdc-boundaries` reproduces the stream and checks every offset. The
last offset is the mandatory end-of-file cut.

## Node boundaries

The base threshold `B(S)` for stored encoded size `S` (TREE-22) corresponds
to `1/4096` at `MIN_NODE` = 4 096, rising linearly to `1/256` at 32 768,
constant to `MAX_NODE` = 65 536. For an item with stored encoded length
`L`, the comparison is `h < min(2^32, floor(B(S) * L / 8))`. Hashing uses
the full-key encoding, while `S` and `L` use the stored compressed encoding.

| S (bytes) | base probability | B(S) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 0.000244141 | 1048576 |
| 8192 | 0.000767299 | 3295524 |
| 12288 | 0.001290458 | 5542473 |
| 16384 | 0.001813616 | 7789421 |
| 20480 | 0.002336775 | 10036370 |
| 24576 | 0.002859933 | 12283318 |
| 28672 | 0.003383092 | 14530267 |
| 32768 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |
| 49152 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |
| 65536 | 0.003906250 | 16777216 |

Between table rows `B(S)` is linear in `S` and MUST be computed exactly as
`floor((2^20 + (S - 4096) * (2^24 - 2^20) / 28672))` for
`4096 <= S <= 32768`, using integer arithmetic.

Per-item comparison vectors (the threshold includes the item length):

| S (bytes) | L (bytes) | comparison threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 8 | 1048576 |
| 8192 | 48 | 19773144 |
| 16384 | 64 | 62315368 |
| 32768 | 128 | 268435456 |
| 65536 | 65536 | 4294967296 |

The final row saturates at `2^32`; it MUST NOT wrap to zero. A node at
`MAX_NODE` closes unconditionally. An item that would exceed the cap is
re-encoded in a new node before the threshold is computed (TREE-22).

## Layout and physical-intent record vectors

These D-80 vectors complete the byte witnesses for D-77's layout version 2
and D-78's protected physical-intent records. Their fields follow
[`terrane-v1.cddl`](terrane-v1.cddl),
[`../13-bucket-layout.md`](../13-bucket-layout.md) and
[`../17-garbage-collection.md`](../17-garbage-collection.md).
Each input model below uses CBOR diagnostic notation. Whitespace inside a
hexadecimal byte string is insignificant. Empty arrays are explicit values;
omitted fields remain absent, rather than null.

Positive vectors fix canonical encoding and decoding. Negative vectors are
canonical CBOR with an invalid field value; their format decoder MUST
reject them. Journal identities and fixed nonce patterns are codec inputs,
not verified filesystem descriptors or secure production randomness.
An Invalidated journal is a valid record that cannot authorize deletion.

The intent binds pack ID `000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f`, cycle 7 and
physical exclusion epoch 2. Its original lease has epoch 3; the current
recovery lease has epoch 4. These distinct epochs do not rewrite the older
physical exclusion. The deletion delay is 60 seconds and its encoded
elapsed lower bound is 60,000,000,000 nanoseconds. Decoding these claims does
not demonstrate that a backend actually waited or checked current roots.
The original authorization is immutable across operation revisions/phases.

The 181-byte pack and its 148-byte detached-index witness bind the exact
artifact versions shown below. The authorization digest is raw BLAKE3 over
its 640 canonical bytes, without an immutable-content domain prefix:

```text
a5802a8ed186b0f68a32c9277ac30f3a39b67941a548d96f2047c082903f6e8c
```

The matching deletion-operation key is:

```text
gc/7/delete/000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f/404142434445464748494a4b4c4d4e4f505152535455565758595a5b5c5d5e5f
```

Every `DeleteOperation` positive vector is decoded against that exact key.
A mismatched cycle, pack ID, nonce, noncanonical decimal or hexadecimal,
suffix or extra segment MUST be rejected. These records do not have
immutable-content descriptors, and a successful codec round trip grants
no publication, reachability, lease, age or deletion authority.

## Reproduction

The vectors were produced with the reference BLAKE3 and Ed25519
implementations and a hand-written canonical CBOR encoder. A conformance
suite regenerates them from the same inputs; a mismatch in any byte is a
failure of `gate:golden-vectors`.
